subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which macronutrient is the body's main source of energy, especially for high-intensity exercise?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the body's main and most readily available energy source.

questions.q: Which of these is a benefit of regular physical activity for physical health?
options: Reduced risk of coronary heart disease
questions.explain: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and reduces the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: A key reason for performing a warm-up before exercise is to:
options: Increase muscle temperature and reduce injury risk
questions.explain: A warm-up raises muscle temperature and prepares the body, reducing the risk of injury.

questions.q: Which somatotype is muscular and broad-shouldered, often suited to power sports?
questions.explain: Mesomorphs are muscular, broad-shouldered and well suited to strength and power events.

questions.q: Fats are an important nutrient because they:
options: Cannot be stored by the body
Provide a slow-release energy source and insulation
questions.explain: Fats provide a concentrated, slow-release energy store and help insulate the body.

questions.q: Mixing with others and making friends through sport is an example of which type of well-being?
questions.explain: Social well-being involves interacting with others, cooperating and forming friendships.

questions.q: The sit-and-reach test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: Which training method involves explosive bounding, hopping and jumping to develop power?
questions.explain: Plyometric training uses explosive movements to develop muscular power.

questions.q: Gradually making training harder over time so the body keeps adapting is called:
questions.explain: Progressive overload means gradually increasing the demands of training to keep improving.

questions.q: The principle that fitness gains are lost when training stops is known as:
questions.explain: Reversibility means fitness levels decline if training is stopped or reduced.

questions.q: A balanced diet for a performer should mainly consist of which macronutrient by proportion?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates should form the largest proportion of a balanced diet as they fuel activity.

Having excess body fat to the extent that health may be affected
questions.explain: Obesity is an excessive accumulation of body fat that may negatively affect health.
